shower.thought: You spend the first part of your life learning to talk, and the rest of your life learning when to shut up.
Nostalgia is just grief wearing a smile.
We call it "falling asleep" but really we're just too tired to keep pretending to be awake anymore.
The moment you become aware of your own breathing, you can't go back to breathing automatically—consciousness ruins even the things that were working fine without it.
You can't remember most of your life, which means you've already forgotten more of yourself than you currently are.
People assume you're fine because you show up, and you keep showing up because people assume you're fine.
The scariest part of having a good idea is realizing someone else probably had it first.
Time moves faster the less you pay attention to it, which means the busier you get, the quicker your life disappears.
You can't step in the same river twice, but you also can't step in a different river—by the time you step, it's not the river you saw anymore.
Confidence is just being wrong with certainty.
We spend our entire childhood wishing we were older, and our entire adulthood wishing we were younger—we never actually want to be the age we are.
The people you love most are the ones who can hurt you the most, which is a pretty terrible trade-off when you think about it.
You only get one perspective of the world, but you live your entire life believing it's the normal one.
Distance doesn't make memories fade—it's the accumulation of new moments that buries the old ones under layers of fresh experience.
Every conversation you have changes you slightly, which means you're technically a different person by the end of it.
The worst part about being smart enough to understand something is realizing you can't unknow it.
We treat time like money, but we only have a limited amount and we're guaranteed to run out—yet somehow we're way more careful with money.
You can't see your own face without a mirror, which means there's a version of you that only exists in other people's memories.
Sleeping is just your body forcing you to stop pretending everything is under control.
Your laugh is the only thing you've never actually heard yourself do.

darkjoke.thought:
My therapist asked why I never talk about my feelings.
I said, "Because every time I do, you write it down and bill me for it."

I told my doctor I was having suicidal thoughts.
He said, "That'll be $200."
I said, "What if I can't afford it?"
He said, "We can work out a payment plan."

My wife left me because I'm too pessimistic.
Well, I say "left." She probably just got lost trying to find the door.

I said to my friend, "I feel like nobody listens to me."
He said, "That's nice," while scrolling his phone.

My job is killing me.
Literally. The commute adds three hours to my day.
At this rate, I'll be dead before my student loans are paid off.

I asked my dad why he never came to my soccer games.
He said, "I was always there. You just never looked in the woods."

My bank called to say they were concerned about my account activity.
Turns out "activity" is a generous word for what I do with my money.

I told my friend I was thinking about getting therapy.
He said, "Finally, someone professional will have to listen to you."

The doctor told me I had six months to live.
I said, "I can't pay your bill."
He said, "Make it a year."

I'm on a seafood diet.
I see food and remember I can't afford it.

My mother always said I'd never amount to anything.
She was right. I'm currently worth exactly nothing.

I asked my gym trainer if I'd ever get the body I wanted.
He said, "Sure, just keep paying membership fees for another ten years."

My therapist says I need to face my demons.
I told him I'm not ready to see my family again.

I told my boss I had a personal emergency.
He asked if it was important.
I said, "More important than you'll ever be."

I failed my driving test three times.
The examiner said, "Maybe you're just not meant to drive."
I said, "That's fair. I've failed at everything else."

My girlfriend said she needed space.
I gave her the entire apartment.
I'm in the garage now.

I told my counselor I was struggling with self-worth.
She said, "Your insurance covers three sessions."
Apparently that's also my worth to them.

My friend said depression was all in my head.
I said, "Exactly. And there's a lot of real estate up there."

I asked my mother why she had me.
She said it was an accident.
I said, "Finally, something we agree on."

The suicide hotline put me on hold.
I said, "This is exactly what I needed."
They said, "Your call is important to us."
I said, "Then why am I listening to jazz?"
